results.summary_before: This project implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier in Verilog that takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product. It is tested with a Cocotb testbench that applies various input combinations and checks the output against expected values. The design uses only the Tiny Tapeout pins and requires no external hardware. It appears to be an educational exercise in structural digital design, with detailed documentation of the partial product generation and summation process.
results.summary: This project implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier in Verilog that takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product. It is tested with a Cocotb testbench that applies various input combinations and checks the output against expected values. The design uses only the Tiny Tapeout pins and requires no external hardware. The documentation details the partial product generation and column-wise summation process.

results.summary_before: This design is a RISC-V based system that boots from an SPI flash memory in XIP mode and executes instructions from there. It provides GPIO pins that can be used for various purposes, such as bitbanged UART. The design is tested with a testbench that includes a model of an SPI flash, and it can be run using FuseSoC. External hardware requires a compatible SPI flash memory.

results.summary_before: This design sums eight input signals, treating them as the numbers 1 through 10, and displays the last digit of the sum on a 7-segment display. It uses eight inputs and eight outputs, with the outputs connected to the segments of the display. The project is intended as a simple test or educational example, and it requires an external 7-segment display to show the result. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the basic operation.

results.summary_before: The design is a resubmission of a simple VGA ray casting game engine that renders textured walls in a 3D-like first-person view without a framebuffer. It is controlled via an SPI interface for player point-of-view and other visual effects registers, and outputs standard VGA signals. Optional external QSPI memory can supply textures, and the chip includes debug and demo modes. This is a more complex design occupying 6x2 tiles and represents an iterative development from earlier Tiny Tapeout versions.

results.summary_before: This design implements a multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit for 2x2 matrix multiplication with 4-bit operands, intended for neural network applications. It includes control signals for write, read, clear, and accumulation enable. Testing involves providing matrices and observing the output, which is read in two 8-bit parts. The design is inspired by existing matrix-MAC units and requires a personal computer for control.
